title: ChatGPT Ads in 2026: What the Early Tests Reveal

facts.fact: OpenAI says it is starting to test ads inside ChatGPT, with the first rollout limited to users in the United States on the Free and Go plans.
facts.value: United States; Free and Go plans
facts.quote: The company says it is starting to test ads inside the product. This first rollout is limited to users in the United States on the Free and Go plans, while Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise remain ad-free.

facts.fact: According to the page, Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise ChatGPT plans remain ad-free during the initial ad test.
facts.quote: while Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise remain ad-free.

facts.fact: OpenAI previewed its ChatGPT ad direction publicly in January 2026, describing the program as a small test with firm guardrails.
facts.quote: OpenAI previewed this direction publicly in January 2026, describing the program as a small test with firm guardrails.

facts.fact: ChatGPT ads appear after the response in a clearly labeled sponsored section below the answer, and the response itself is unchanged.
facts.quote: When an ad appears, it shows up after ChatGPT responds, in a clearly labeled sponsored section below the answer. The response itself is unchanged.

facts.fact: OpenAI states that ads do not influence how ChatGPT responses are generated.
facts.quote: OpenAI has also stated that ads **do not influence** how responses are generated.

facts.fact: Users under 18 are excluded from seeing ChatGPT ads, according to OpenAI's described guardrails.
facts.quote: Users under 18 are excluded, and ads will be kept out of sensitive categories such as health, mental health, and politics.

facts.fact: ChatGPT ads are kept out of sensitive categories such as health, mental health, and politics.
facts.quote: ads will be kept out of sensitive categories such as health, mental health, and politics.

facts.fact: OpenAI describes ChatGPT ad matching as contextual to the conversation rather than based on advertiser access to user profiles, with ads matched on conversation topic and intent signals.
facts.quote: OpenAI describes ad matching as contextual to the conversation, rather than built around advertiser access to user profiles.

facts.fact: Advertisers in early ChatGPT ad tests receive basic aggregated reporting showing how many times an ad was shown and how many times it was interacted with.
facts.quote: What advertisers can see today is basic, aggregated reporting. That typically includes how many times an ad was shown and how many times it was interacted with.

facts.fact: Advertisers in early ChatGPT ad tests receive no user-level data, demographics, or interest profiles.
facts.quote: There is no user-level data. There are no demographics, no interest profiles, and no visibility into who saw an ad beyond the aggregate counts.

facts.fact: ChatGPT ads have no standard conversion tracking or attribution path, so advertisers cannot follow a user from a conversation to a later purchase or signup.
facts.quote: There is no standard conversion tracking or attribution path, and advertisers cannot follow a user from a conversation to a later purchase or signup.

facts.fact: ChatGPT does not allow tracking pixels, third-party trackers, or external analytics integrations for ads, which OpenAI frames as a deliberate design choice.
facts.quote: It does not allow tracking pixels, third-party trackers, or external analytics integrations, and OpenAI has framed that as a deliberate design choice.

facts.fact: Early reporting suggests ChatGPT ads may be priced on a CPM basis, though the page does not state any specific rate.
facts.quote: Early reporting suggests ChatGPT ads may be priced on a CPM basis
